findings.remediation: Grant write scopes only to the job that needs them and keep all other scopes read-only or none.
findings.impact: A compromised workflow step can modify repository content, packages, deployments, checks, or security records within the granted scope.
findings.attack_vector: A permissions block grants a named write scope; exploitability depends on whether untrusted code reaches that job.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: references 2 action or reusable workflow ref(s) that are not pinned to a full commit SHA
findings.remediation: Pin third-party actions and reusable workflows to a full 40-character commit SHA.
findings.impact: Mutable action refs can change without a workflow diff if the upstream tag or branch is moved.
findings.attack_vector: A workflow uses @main, @master, a version tag, or another ref instead of a full commit SHA.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: attempts path traversal with encoded or nested patterns
findings.remediation: Use path.resolve() and verify the result stays within the workspace root.
findings.impact: Path traversal with encoded patterns (%2e%2e%2f) or nested ../.. can escape any path-based sandbox.
findings.attack_vector: URL-encoded or nested traversal sequences — bypass naive path validation that only checks single ../.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: contains multiple layers of encoding (hex/base64/unicode escapes)
findings.remediation: Avoid multi-layer encoding; it hindles review and may indicate malicious intent.
findings.impact: Multi-layer encoding (hex/base64/unicode) significantly hinders security review.
findings.attack_vector: Chained decoding layers — attacker increases analysis cost and may hide malicious payloads.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: contains 1 line(s) longer than 500 characters (possible minified/obfuscated code)
findings.remediation: Review extremely long lines; they may contain hidden logic.
findings.impact: Extremely long lines hide obfuscated or minified code from human review.
findings.attack_vector: Lines > 500 chars — code is structured to evade visual inspection.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: constructs a regular expression from a non-literal value (possible ReDoS)
findings.basis: OWASP Regular Expression Denial of Service Prevention
findings.remediation: Use bounded, allowlisted patterns and enforce input and execution limits for dynamic regular expressions.
findings.impact: An attacker-controlled regular expression can consume excessive CPU and deny service.
findings.attack_vector: A non-literal value is passed to RegExp without pattern or execution bounds.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: uses eval() or new Function() to execute dynamically generated code
findings.remediation: Remove dynamic evaluation and use fixed allowlisted implementations.
findings.impact: Dynamic eval/Function executes code that is difficult to audit and becomes code injection if external input reaches it.
findings.attack_vector: Source uses eval()/new Function(); this rule alone does not prove that an attacker controls the evaluated value.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: uses Error.stack or stack trace inspection for anti-debugging
findings.remediation: Avoid stack-based anti-debugging techniques; they indicate malicious intent.
findings.impact: Stack inspection can support anti-analysis behavior, but is also common in diagnostics and error reporting.
findings.attack_vector: Source reads Error.stack or invokes a trace helper; reviewer must determine intent.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.remediation: Require explicit user approval and restrict mutations to an allowlisted workspace path.
findings.downgrade: Downgraded from high: no system-impact pattern matched near the call site.
findings.impact: Unbounded file-system mutations can overwrite critical files, install backdoors, or corrupt data.
findings.attack_vector: writeFile/mkdir/chmod without workspace boundary check — path is not validated against workspace root.
findings.risk_adjustment: Explicit risk (medium) set by caller; evidence-based risk adjustment skipped.
